title: Boku no Hero Academia: Final Season
content:
It took 9.5 years for everyone to take the new-gen “Naruto” seriously, as it was labeled back in 2016 and even prior in the Manga sphere. The show wasn’t always great, but damn it did it have some iconic and very memorable highs.

I’m gonna address the length first and move on. I felt like we were robbed with this being only eleven episodes. The tension that the show left off with at the end of season seven was immense and hard to met, and surprisingly, for the most part, the final season did touch on some of those expectations, but it really did rush the topping in my eyes. The cake was still delicious.

Controversial as it might be, the ending did deliver on what the first season was alluding to. Plot points were resolved and characters had their self-centric arcs, but man, the imminent death flags that a few characters had circling them for multiple seasons look so  pathetic in hinside. I mean, I love those characters, but come on, the narrative would have benefited so much more if the Mangaka was committed to the causes and effect he himself decided. i guess the show wanted to leave off a certain legacy and it did. There is even a bit of open-endedness that leaves us off in the last episode, so here’s a dose of hope to that.

I won’t say this was the best season in My Hero’s arsenal, but it did had some of the best fights and character moments and that’s a huge plus. This is a strong rewatch.

Overall: 8.64/10.
